user_prompt:
What is the effect of fibrin-based haemostatic agents (fibrin sealant, fibrin glue, fibrin patches or fibrin-coated collagen), compared with other haemostatic agents or techniques that are not fibrin-based (for example oxidised cellulose, collagen sponges, argon beam coagulation, electrocautery, or standard surgical haemostasis), on perioperative mortality in adults undergoing liver resection?

Effect measure: pool as a risk ratio (RR) of death, fibrin-based agent divided by the non-fibrin comparator, using a random-effects model. RR > 1 means more deaths with the fibrin-based agent.

Outcome: number of participants who died during the perioperative period (events) out of the number randomised to each arm (total). Perioperative means in hospital or within about 30 to 90 days of the operation, as each paper defines it.
- Count deaths from any cause. Do not use treatment-related deaths only, and do not use late mortality at one year or more.
- If a paper reports that no deaths occurred in an arm, record zero events with the arm size; if it does not report mortality at all, leave the trial out.
- Use the number randomised as the denominator (intention-to-treat). If the paper reports the number in the safety or treated population only, use that and state it.
- Multi-arm trials: include the fibrin-based arm and one non-fibrin comparator arm. If a trial has two non-fibrin arms, combine them into one control group (sum events and participants).
- Assign arms by treatment description, not by column position.
- Include only randomised controlled trials in adults undergoing liver (hepatic) resection. Exclude trials comparing a fibrin agent with no haemostatic agent at all (they belong to a different comparison), comparisons of two fibrin agents, and non-randomised studies.

Do not pool blood loss, time to haemostasis, transfusion, bile leak, reoperation, infection or any other outcome.
